evidence: The surviving solutions build an adjacency list and perform tree-style processing; both rely on the statement's guarantee that all n variables become equal when all n-1 constraints are enforced.
affordance_in_statement: The list of constraints is minimally exhaustive: there are exactly m = n − 1 available constraints, and if you were to enforce every single one of them, all n variables would be forced to take the exact same value.
removal_suggestion: There is no safe wording-only removal: with pairwise equality constraints, positive costs, m = n − 1, and the guarantee that all variables become equal, the underlying graph is necessarily a tree and the minimum solution is intrinsically the unique subtree connecting the targets. Defeating this shortcut would require allowing a general connected graph or changing the constraint semantics.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the constraints as a tree and computes the cost of the target-induced connecting subtree using adjacency-list traversal.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: There are exactly m = n − 1 available constraints, and enforcing every single one forces all n variables to be equal.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the same tree representation and target-marking/pruning approach to retain only edges needed to connect target variables.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The only way to guarantee that two variables are equal is to link them through a sequence of enforced constraints.

common_affordance: The constraints form a connected tree, so connecting all targets reduces intrinsically to selecting the unique minimal subtree containing them.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its DFS-based needed-node propagation is incorrect on some tree configurations, so it does not reliably retain exactly the edges in the target-induced subtree.

Its DSU/Kruskal-style approach treats the task like a generic minimum-spanning connection problem and can include edges leading to irrelevant non-target branches instead of using the unique target subtree.

recommended_edit: No admissible single edit can defeat both survivors while preserving the immutable input bounds, pairwise-equality semantics, and task. The only effective change would be to present the constraints as a general connected graph with redundant links or otherwise change the constraint model, which changes the structural problem.
regression_risk: Any edit that merely obscures the tree guarantee could accidentally make the already-defeated DFS or DSU implementations appear correct on the affected cases.
